extrait: ARISTOTLE ON VOLUNTARINESS OF INTEMPERANCE VS COWARDICE  This chapter returns to the theme of voluntariness, arguing that intemperance is MORE voluntary than cowardice, which has implications for moral responsibility.  Greek: ἑκουσίῳ δὲ μᾶλ

ARISTOTLE ON DELIBERATION AND THE SCOPE OF HUMAN AGENCY  This chapter defines the domain of deliberation and thereby the scope of τὸ ἐφʼ ἡμῖν (what is up to us) - the crucial concept for all subsequent free will debates.  Greek: βουλεύονται

ARISTOTLE'S ANALYSIS OF PROHAIRESIS (DELIBERATE CHOICE)  Having defined voluntary action, Aristotle now analyzes προαίρεσις - the distinctively human capacity for rational choice that is most closely connected to virtue and character.  Gree

ARISTOTLE ON WISH AND THE APPEARANCE OF THE GOOD  This chapter addresses a fundamental question: Is the object of wish the real good or the apparent good? The answer has implications for moral responsibility.  Greek: ἡ δὲ βούλησις ὅτι μὲν τ
